summary: Missing maxBatch configuration causes worker chunking to evaluate to NaN, producing empty chunks and losing all batch items.

findings.title: Undefined maxBatch in config causes chunking loop failure and data loss
findings.body: src/worker.js relies on config.maxBatch to slice batch IDs into chunks, but config/default.json does not define maxBatch. In JavaScript, accessing this undefined property causes i + config.maxBatch to produce NaN. As a result, ids.slice(0, NaN) returns [] and i becomes NaN, terminating the loop after a single iteration and returning [[]] as chunks regardless of the input.
findings.recommendation: Define maxBatch in config/default.json and specify a fallback or validation in src/worker.js (e.g., const maxBatch = config.maxBatch ?? 100).

samples.summary: Missing maxBatch configuration causes drain() in worker.js to slice with undefined bounds and drop all items.

findings.title: Undefined config.maxBatch causes chunking failure and data loss in worker.js
findings.body: config.maxBatch is referenced in src/worker.js (lines 7-9) to chunk validated batch IDs, but maxBatch is not defined in config/default.json. Consequently, config.maxBatch is undefined at runtime, causing ids.slice(i, i + config.maxBatch) to evaluate to ids.slice(0, NaN) which returns [] and i += config.maxBatch to become NaN. This terminates the loop after a single iteration and silently discards all IDs.
findings.recommendation: Add the maxBatch property to config/default.json and specify a fallback in src/worker.js (e.g., const maxBatch = config.maxBatch || 100).

samples.summary: Worker chunking fails due to undefined config.maxBatch dropping all batch items, and legacy v1 validate logic remains a stale duplicate unpatched against missing IDs.

findings.title: Undefined config.maxBatch causes chunking failure and data loss in worker
findings.body: src/worker.js references config.maxBatch in the chunking loop at lines 7-9, but maxBatch is not defined in config/default.json. Because config.maxBatch is undefined, ids.slice(0, NaN) yields an empty array and i becomes NaN, immediately terminating the loop and returning chunks: [[]], discarding all items in the batch.
findings.recommendation: Define maxBatch in config/default.json and add fallback validation in src/worker.js (e.g. const maxBatch = Number(config.maxBatch) || 100).

findings.title: Stale duplicate validation in v1 missing null-safe filtering for batch items
findings.body: The fix to skip entries with missing IDs was applied to src/api/v2/validate.js, but src/api/v1/validate.js remains a stale duplicate that calls batch.map((item) => String(item.id)). If legacy clients send batch items that are null, undefined, or missing an id property, v1 will throw a TypeError and abort processing the entire batch.
findings.recommendation: Update src/api/v1/validate.js to filter out null or missing id items matching v2, or consolidate shared validation logic into a common helper.
